headline: Record margin and backlog despite flat organic revenue
summary_short: Revenue rose 2% to $1.7B (down 1% organically) while adjusted EBITDA hit a record $168M at a 10.2% margin. Total backlog reached a record $9.4B with a 1.1x book-to-bill.
summary_long: Excluding a confidential contract, revenue grew 5% and organic revenue 2%, led by Cyber and Electronic Warfare and Transportation. Operating income fell 4% to $104M on higher transaction-related expenses. Contract awards rose 14% and Federal Solutions awards 53%. Parsons narrowed 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance while reiterating the midpoint. Separately, the CFO is resigning effective November 6, with George Ball as interim CFO.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS are non-GAAP. GAAP EPS delta computed from $0.51 versus $0.59. The CFO transition was announced in a separate release the same day.

drivers.explanation: Growth in Cyber and Electronic Warfare and Transportation markets, excluding the impact of a confidential contract.
Higher transaction-related expenses reduced operating income and net income.
Accretive growth across both the Critical Infrastructure and Federal Solutions segments.
CEO says strong awards, record backlog and a robust pipeline support continued organic growth, while procurement timing and geopolitical uncertainty persist.
